newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico stocks rally to new record close.
newsitem.headline: Mexico stocks rally to new record close.

text.p: Mexican stocks gained sharply on Thursday to chalk up their second record close in a row, and their sixth for the month so far.
Dealers and analysts said share prices rallied on agressive buying by foreign investors, spurred by a skyrocketing Dow Jones and fortuitous economic news.
"Yesterday's rally confirmed the market's upside expectations," said Inverlat brokerage analyst Hector Jimenez.
Final closing prices situated the IPC share index up 45.58 points, or 1.09 percent, at 4,240.02.
Volume was very heavy at 183.33 million shares traded.
"We have seen heavy foreign investment with a long-term view and I feel a good outcome to the elections has also been discounted," Jimenez added.
Many traders and analysts put the bourse's recent gains down to a "virtuous circle" of domestic and international economic data, the Dow Jones and fixed-income markets.
The Dow Jones closed up 135.64 points to 7,711.47.

"For a start, I feel (Tuesday's) primary auction went down well and the market could also be discounting a decision to leave no U.S. rates unchanged at the July 2 Federal Open Market Committee meeting," a stock promoter said, who asked not to be named.
Dealers said low returns on fixed-income instruments made many investors switch to stock markets.
U.S. 30-year Treasury bonds were down 26/32 in late trade to yield 6.78 percent. Mexican overnight Cetes rates closed down 205 basis points to 19.35 percent.
The promotor said heavily weighted blue chips like Telmex and Grupo Carso led the charge.
Telmex gained 8 centavos to 19.00 pesos, while the telecomms firm's ADRs ended up 1/2 to 48. Holding company Grupo Carso gained 1.00 pesos to 48.80 pesos.

On the broad market, a total of 121 stocks changed hands, of which 70 gained while 26 fell. Mining company Grupo Mexico L series headed the prominent gainers list, up 3.45 pesos to 25.45 pesos on news Asrco had sold 20 million of the shares in early trade.
